name: screen_read
summary: Read what a ScriptedScreens screen shows (a Console or Computer board, a tablet, a visor): its surfaces and one surface's elements with their boxes, text and props, from the host's model. image adds a PNG where the game draws. Read only.

help.text: The model is the elements the chip's script has built, as the host holds them, so it works on a dedicated server. Each element gives id, type, box {x, y, w, h} in surface pixels from the top-left (null when it needs a surface size the script did not set), shown, touch (a control screen_press can touch) and props (text, value, z_index...). A vector element's motion is drawn by each client; its props hold the scene. image true asks ScriptedScreens for its own picture of the drawn surface, which a dedicated server cannot give (not_rendered).
help.keys: holder {reference_id, prefab_name, display_name}, chip_id, surfaces [{name, element_count, shown_on}], surface, width, height, elements [{id, type, box, shown, touch, props, style}], count, total, offset, limit, has_more, image {path, surface, width, height}.

refusals.summary: Why a screen cannot be read.
refusals.text: screens_mod_required (ScriptedScreens is not loaded); screens_changed (a ScriptedScreens version StationGod cannot read); no_screen (the chip has drawn nothing, or the holder is not a ScriptedScreens host); surface_not_found (the message lists the surfaces); not_rendered and capture_failed (image only).

surface.description: The surface to list; default the one the main screen shows.

type.description: Only elements of this type (button, label, gauge...).

text_contains.description: Only elements whose text, label, title, placeholder or value holds this, any case.

shown_only.description: Default true: leave out hidden elements and those inside hidden ones.

include_style.description: true: add each element's style (colours, fonts). Default false.

image.description: true: add a PNG of the drawn surface (not on a dedicated server).
